title: MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization
summary: It replaces fixed-granularity KV cache quantization policies (uniform layer-wise or token-wise precision assignment) with a profiling-guided allocator that splits a fixed KV memory budget between layer-wise precision enhancement and token-wise preservation. The cost is a one-time offline profiling pass to estimate layer sensitivity and token importance, plus implementation complexity for mixed-granularity quantization; there is no online search overhead at inference. It can fail if the profiling distribution diverges from production traffic (token-importance and layer-sensitivity estimates may not transfer), if the serving stack lacks kernels supporting mixed per-layer and per-token precision, or if the abstract's unquantified gains do not replicate on the reader's model and workload.
rationale: The approach targets exactly the reader's constraint (a fixed KV memory budget on a single GPU) and avoids online search, but the claim is unquantified and the benefit depends on workload-specific profiling and kernel support, so it merits a small-scale validation before production adoption.
